Well, it is, for quite some time, but eventually, you run out of things that actively engage you, that aren't people. It's very expensive to change exhibits out, so it doesn't happen very often; that means most of your intellectual stimulation has to be self-provided, or shared with guests. It's definitely waaaay over-exaggerated on TV! That's not to say it's boring, because it isn't really, but me doing my job doesn't look that much different from any programmer doing his job, really. Except the office I work in looks a lot more sciency with large microscopes and intimidating looking machines sitting around. Basically when you watch CSI or one of those shows, I would be the guy the wrote the software the technicians are using for analyzing samples.

Of course I get to go to the labs where the software actually is being used, as well. It's a lot less exciting than you would imagine. There's a very rigid set of steps they go through, just to end up with a bunch of numbers that basically tell the chance that this person is who they think it is, and so on. Doing a case takes many hours, and they are often doing several of them at once, and don't know much or worry much about they actual case they are working on. It's all about following the proper procedures so that the results are correct.

But again, the labs do look pretty cool, TV does a good job of getting that part across!

One of the issues with Project Gutenberg is that over the years they say that they stand for a free and open internet, free-flow of information, protecting the public domain, and how they are concerned about the TPP, but they don't always practice what they preach.

For one thing, they actively block people that use VPN's, TOR, and other proxy systems, forcing you to expose yourself online, yet they don't use any form of encryption to protect those that use the platform, which puts users' information at risk of being taken, used, and possibly abused by outside entities.

It is kind of two-faced to say that you want to protect internet rights, while actively behaving in a way that undermines those principles. There are better ways of ensuring that users are human.

Is it detrimental? No, not totally, but it is important enough to bring up to people who are considering using the site.
